drills.q: Why is post-retrieval ACL filtering in application code a security problem, not just a recall problem?
drills.a: It under-returns when the allowed subset is small (recall issue), and any code path that skips the discard step leaks another tenant's data outright -- a breach, not a quality bug.

drills.q: Compare Pinecone namespaces vs Weaviate per-tenant shards for multi-tenancy.
drills.a: Pinecone namespaces are a cheap logical partition scaling to 100K+ tenants but not cryptographic isolation. Weaviate gives each tenant a physically separate HNSW shard for stronger isolation, at the cost of per-shard overhead for tiny tenants (mitigated by cold storage).

drills.q: Why can't you fix a PII leak by filtering the model's output after generation?
drills.a: The PII was already retrieved and placed in context before generation -- output filtering can't undo its influence on the response, and paraphrased PII can slip past pattern-matching filters even when ingestion-time redaction would have caught the original text.

drills.q: Walk through a zero-downtime migration for switching embedding models.
drills.a: Build the new index fully in parallel; dual-write new/changed docs to both during the build window; validate against a golden query set; atomically swap an alias with instant rollback available; retain the old index for a bounded window (~24h) before decommissioning.

drills.q: What's the risk of a nightly batch ACL sync between a source permission system and a RAG index?
drills.a: A staleness window up to the sync interval exists between a permission revocation and it taking effect in retrieval, during which a revoked user can still see documents they should no longer access. Fix with webhook-driven near-real-time sync.

drills.q: Break down where cost actually goes in a production RAG query and where you'd optimize first.
drills.a: Embedding and vector search are cheap; reranking is moderate; generation (context+question+answer tokens) dominates. Optimize generation model choice and retrieval precision (smaller, better-targeted context) before touching vector search infrastructure.

drills.q: Design the multi-tenant retrieval architecture for a SaaS product where tenants range from a handful of documents to millions.
drills.a: No single strategy fits both ends: small tenants can share a logically-partitioned index cheaply (low query volume, low noisy-neighbor risk); large tenants benefit from physical shard isolation to avoid noisy neighbors and filtered-search recall problems. An adaptive strategy by tenant size/volume threshold is the honest answer, with the added complexity of a migration path when a tenant crosses it.

drills.q: A corpus changes continuously at thousands of updates/hour with a 5-minute searchability SLA. Design the incremental indexing strategy.
drills.a: Batch reindexing can't meet the SLA; use streaming ingestion directly into the live index (HNSW supports native incremental insert). Deletes/updates get tombstoned, not cleanly removed, so schedule periodic compaction/rebuild based on monitored tombstone ratio and query-quality metrics rather than a fixed interval.
